name: Body Perception Questionnaire
description: The Body Perception Questionnaire (BPQ) assesses body awareness and autonomic nervous system reactivity. It measures interoceptive awareness - the ability to sense internal body signals.
instructions: Below are several statements about how aware you are of your body during your normal daily life. Please rate each item on how true it is for you during an average day.

questions.text: During most situations I am aware of my heart rate.
I notice changes in my breathing when I am excited.
I notice the flow of air in and out of my mouth when I breathe.
I can feel my hands and feet becoming warm.
I notice when I'm having a strong emotional reaction to something.
I notice where in my body I am most comfortable.
I notice where in my body I am most uncomfortable.
I notice distinct body sensations that reflect my mood.
I notice body sensations that come with being relaxed.
I notice how my body changes when I am angry.
I notice when I am uncomfortable in my body.
I notice when there is a pleasant feeling in my body.
I am aware of the flow of my breath.
I can feel my heart beating.
I am able to sense where the tension is located in my body.
I notice when my muscles are tired.
I notice when my muscles are tense.
I am aware of changes in my body temperature.
I notice when I am hungry.
I feel my body is an important source of information for me.
I pay attention to sensations in my body.
I can locate where I feel uncomfortable in my body.
I feel it is important to maintain awareness of my body.
I listen to my body to advise me about what to do.
When I am upset, I take time to explore how my body feels.
I can locate where I feel pleasant sensations in my body.
During the last week, I have had stomach problems (such as nausea, indigestion, 'butterflies').
During the last week, I have felt my heart beating rapidly.
During the last week, I have felt lightheaded or dizzy.
During the last week, I have felt tense.
During the last week, I have had pain or aching in my muscles.
During the last week, I have felt trembling or shaky.
During the last week, I have had difficulty breathing.
During the last week, I have felt chest discomfort.
During the last week, I have felt faint.
During the last week, I have felt hot or cold sweats.
During the last week, I have felt numbness or tingling.
During the last week, I have had diarrhea or constipation.
During the last week, I have felt tired.
During the last week, I have had headaches.
During the last week, I have felt weak in parts of my body.
During the last week, I have had problems swallowing.
During the last week, I have felt eye strain.
During the last week, I have had back pain.
During the last week, I have felt restless.
During the last week, I have had difficulty sleeping.

body-awareness.label: Body Awareness
body-awareness.description: Awareness of internal body sensations and interoceptive signals

autonomic-reactivity.label: Autonomic Nervous System Reactivity
autonomic-reactivity.description: Physical symptoms reflecting autonomic nervous system activity over the past week

severityBands.label: Low Body Awareness
severityBands.description: Low interoceptive awareness; may have difficulty recognizing internal body signals.
severityBands.recommendation: Consider body-based practices such as mindfulness, yoga, or interoceptive training to improve body awareness.

severityBands.label: Moderate Body Awareness
severityBands.description: Moderate interoceptive awareness with room for improvement.
severityBands.recommendation: Continue developing body awareness through regular mindful attention to internal sensations.

severityBands.label: High Body Awareness
severityBands.description: Good interoceptive awareness; able to recognize and interpret internal body signals effectively.

severityBands.label: Low Autonomic Reactivity
severityBands.description: Few autonomic symptoms reported; good autonomic regulation.

severityBands.label: Moderate Autonomic Reactivity
severityBands.description: Some autonomic symptoms present; may indicate mild stress or dysregulation.
severityBands.recommendation: Consider stress reduction techniques and lifestyle modifications.

severityBands.label: High Autonomic Reactivity
severityBands.description: Significant autonomic symptoms; may indicate stress, anxiety, or autonomic dysregulation.
severityBands.recommendation: Clinical evaluation recommended. Consider interventions targeting autonomic regulation such as biofeedback, breathing exercises, or medical evaluation.

body-awareness-total.label: Body Awareness Total
body-awareness-total.interpretation: Higher scores indicate greater body awareness and interoceptive sensitivity

autonomic-reactivity-total.label: Autonomic Reactivity Total
autonomic-reactivity-total.interpretation: Higher scores indicate more autonomic symptoms and potential dysregulation

cardiac-awareness.label: Cardiac Awareness
cardiac-awareness.interpretation: Awareness of heart rate and heartbeat

emotional-awareness.label: Emotional Body Awareness
emotional-awareness.interpretation: Awareness of body sensations associated with emotions

riskRules.message: Elevated autonomic symptoms may indicate stress, anxiety, or need for medical evaluation.
Low body awareness may benefit from interoceptive training or body-based therapies.
Frequent cardiac symptoms reported; consider cardiac evaluation if persistent.
Frequent breathing difficulties reported; further evaluation recommended.
High fatigue and sleep difficulties reported; consider sleep evaluation.

interpretation.summary: The BPQ measures two main constructs: Body Awareness (interoceptive sensitivity - the ability to sense internal body signals) and Autonomic Nervous System Reactivity (physical symptoms reflecting autonomic function). These constructs are relevant to understanding mind-body integration and somatic health.
interpretation.clinicalUse: The BPQ is used in research and clinical settings to assess interoceptive awareness, which is relevant to anxiety disorders, depression, PTSD, chronic pain, and other conditions involving body-mind integration.

body-awareness.interpretation: Higher scores indicate greater awareness of internal body sensations. This reflects the capacity for interoceptive attention and sensitivity.

autonomic-reactivity.interpretation: Higher scores indicate more autonomic symptoms over the past week. Elevated scores may reflect stress, anxiety, or autonomic dysregulation.

notes: Body awareness and autonomic reactivity are distinct but related constructs
High body awareness with low reactivity typically reflects healthy interoception
High body awareness with high reactivity may indicate hypervigilance or anxiety
Low body awareness may be associated with alexithymia or dissociation
Autonomic symptoms should be interpreted in the context of medical history
